levels.name: Village Forum
levels.description: A packed-earth square where the village elders hear disputes beneath an open sky. Rome's order begins with a bench and a bell.

levels.name: Town Magistracy
levels.description: A modest hall of brick and tile where an elected magistrate keeps the census rolls and the tax tablets. Litigants queue at dawn.

levels.name: Civic Basilica
levels.description: A colonnaded hall for courts, contracts, and the public treasury. Under its long roof, Roman law becomes a daily habit.

levels.name: Provincial Praetorium
levels.description: The fortified residence of a governing praetor, with clerks, lictors, and a strongroom for the province's silver.

levels.name: Hall of the Proconsul
levels.description: Marble steps, bronze doors, and a proconsul's staff large enough to govern a small kingdom. Petitioners come from a hundred miles away.

levels.name: Imperial Curia
levels.description: A vast complex of courts, archives, and audience chambers fit to rule the world. From here, one man's word can reach every shore of the sea.

levels.name: Village Assembly
levels.description: Freeholders gather at the threshing floor to vote by show of hands. Even the smallest kome insists on having its say.

levels.name: Bouleuterion
levels.description: A stepped council chamber where the boule debates grain prices and city walls. Argument is the Hellene's favorite public work.

levels.name: Prytaneion
levels.description: The city's ceremonial hearth, where presiding officers dine honored guests and the sacred fire never goes out.

levels.name: Archon's Hall
levels.description: Chief magistrates administer courts, festivals, and the fleet levy from a stoa-fronted hall in the agora's best corner.

levels.name: Strategeion
levels.description: The seat of the generals-in-office, joining civic government to military command. Maps, muster rolls, and ambition fill its rooms.

levels.name: Basileion
levels.description: A royal palace in the grand successor style: audience courts, treasuries, and gardens meant to overawe ambassadors before they speak.

levels.name: Headman's Hall
levels.description: The village headman judges quarrels over water rights from a carpeted platform. His word carries because his memory is long.

levels.name: Citadel Court
levels.description: A walled court below the town's citadel where scribes tally tribute in grain, horses, and silver.

levels.name: Satrapal Residence
levels.description: The house of the king's appointed governor, half fortress and half archive, keeping the royal road's messengers supplied.

levels.name: Satrapal Palace
levels.description: Glazed brick and cedar beams announce that the king's eye rests here. Provincial nobles attend its court or answer for their absence.

levels.name: Apadana Hall
levels.description: A pillared audience hall in the old Persian manner, where a hundred delegations can wait upon the throne at once.

levels.name: Palace of the King of Kings
levels.description: Terraced gardens, fire altars, and treasuries deep enough to buy an army outright. Lesser kings kneel in its forecourt.

levels.name: Village Council
levels.description: Landowners and shipmasters meet under an awning to settle debts and harbor dues. Everything is written down twice.

levels.name: Suffet's Court
levels.description: An elected suffet dispenses judgment beside the weighing stones. Punic justice is brisk, commercial, and final.

levels.name: Council of Elders
levels.description: The town's wealthiest families sit in permanent council, balancing the fleet's needs against the countinghouse's caution.

levels.name: Tribunal of the Hundred
levels.description: A standing court of a hundred judges audits generals and governors alike. No commander sails home without an accounting.

levels.name: Palace of the Suffetes
levels.description: Twin magistrates govern from a purple-hung hall above the harbor, where trade treaties are sealed with silver and salt.

levels.name: Byrsa Citadel
levels.description: A citadel-crowned acropolis of archives, mints, and council chambers — the commanding height of a merchant empire.

levels.name: Overseer's House
levels.description: The overseer of fields keeps flood records and settles boundary quarrels once the waters recede. The measuring rope decides all.

levels.name: Nomarch's Court
levels.description: The district governor's court, where scribes reckon the harvest tax to the last basket of emmer.

levels.name: Nomarch's Residence
levels.description: A whitewashed compound of offices, granaries, and shaded courts. The nome is governed by ink, not iron.

levels.name: Dioiketes' Hall
levels.description: The royal finance minister's provincial seat, running the most thorough tax machine in the known world.

levels.name: Royal Enclosure
levels.description: A walled precinct of palaces and chancelleries where Greek ministers and Egyptian priests uneasily share power.

levels.name: Pharaoh's Palace
levels.description: Colossal gateways and gilded halls proclaim the living god's rule. The Nile itself seems to flow at the palace's pleasure.

levels.name: Chieftain's Roundhouse
levels.description: The chief holds court by his hearth, flanked by sworn companions. Judgment comes with mead, and sometimes with a spear.

levels.name: Clan Moot Hall
levels.description: A long timber hall where clan heads gather to swear oaths, divide plunder, and choose who leads the summer's raiding.

levels.name: War-King's Longhouse
levels.description: Carved pillars and captured standards line the hall of a king who commands many clans. His household warriors keep a rough peace.

levels.name: Great Oppidum Hall
levels.description: The high seat of a fortified tribal capital, minting its own coin and treating with foreign envoys. The tribes bow to no marble.

levels.name: Village Common Hall
levels.description: A shared hall for markets, weddings, and rough justice. The village governs itself because no one else has bothered to.

levels.name: Town Council House
levels.description: Local notables keep the peace and the granary keys, beholden to no distant crown.

levels.name: Free City Chambers
levels.description: A council of merchants and landholders runs the town's affairs, hiring guards when it must and paying tribute when it cannot.

levels.name: Citizens' Assembly Hall
levels.description: An independent city's assembly, proud of its liberty and nervously watching the great powers circle.

levels.name: Grand Civic Hall
levels.description: The polished seat of a wealthy free city that has outlasted three empires by paying two of them.

levels.name: Earth and Stake Rampart
levels.description: A ditch, a bank, and sharpened stakes in the legionary manner. Enough to make raiders think twice.

levels.name: Timber Wall Walk
levels.description: A proper timber curtain with a fighting platform and gate towers. Sentries pace it through the night watches.

levels.name: Ashlar Circuit
levels.description: Cut stone laid without mortar, gates hung with iron-shod oak. The town now expects a siege rather than fears one.

levels.name: Great Ashlar Circuit
levels.description: High double-faced walls with artillery platforms at each tower. Attackers must bring engines, patience, and luck.

levels.name: Colossal Bastions
levels.description: Bastioned walls the height of five men, ringed with towers and sally ports. Armies have starved outside such stone.

levels.name: Rubble Rampart
levels.description: Fieldstone heaped on an earthen bank, patched every spring. It keeps out wolves, bandits, and impatient captains.

levels.name: Mudbrick Wall
levels.description: Thick sun-dried brick on stone footings, cool in summer and stubborn under rams. The gatehouse doubles as a toll station.

levels.name: Cut-Stone Wall
levels.description: Dressed masonry raised by hired engineers, with square towers commanding every approach.

levels.name: Towered Enceinte
levels.description: A full circuit of high walls and artillery towers built to the best Hellenistic theory. Siege masters lecture from its parapets.

levels.name: Triple Wall
levels.description: Three concentric lines of defense with stables and barracks built into the walls themselves. Taking it costs a generation.

levels.name: Ditch and Bank
levels.description: A deep ditch and thorn-topped bank thrown up by the whole village in a season. Simple, and surprisingly effective.

levels.name: Oak Stockade
levels.description: Whole trunks set upright and lashed with iron, with a fighting walk behind. The gate gods get their offerings here.

levels.name: Timber-Laced Rampart
levels.description: Stone and earth bound through with timber beams — a rampart that shrugs off rams and fire alike. Hillfort craft at its best.

levels.name: Muster Field
levels.description: A leveled field with a speaking mound where citizens present themselves with spear and shield when the levy is called.

levels.name: Drill Grounds
levels.description: Practice posts, wooden swords, and a bawling drillmaster. Farm boys leave with straight backs and blistered hands.

levels.name: Manipular Barracks
levels.description: Permanent quarters where maniples learn to open, close, and relieve one another in line. The checkerboard becomes instinct.

levels.name: Legionary Camp
levels.description: A standing camp with armories, smiths, and veteran instructors. Its arsenals send men out better armed than they arrived.

levels.name: Field of Mars
levels.description: A great training ground consecrated to the war god, where whole legions exercise under the eyes of old triarii. Discipline here is a religion.

levels.name: Militia Muster
levels.description: A cleared ground and a rack of spears for the citizen levy. Every able man knows his place in the line, roughly.

levels.name: City Watch Barracks
levels.description: Quarters for a paid town guard who drill in the cool hours and police the market the rest of the day.

levels.name: Soldiers' Quarters
levels.description: Barracks, storerooms, and a drill court for professional infantry. Pike and shield drills raise dust from dawn onward.

levels.name: Royal Barracks
levels.description: A crown-funded garrison complex with its own armories and pay office. Service here is a career, not a season.

levels.name: Palace Guard Barracks
levels.description: The training halls of the household regiments, where the kingdom's best arms and hardest instructors are spent freely.

levels.name: Gathering Ground
levels.description: The field where the war horn summons every able body. Courage is assumed; formation is negotiable.

levels.name: Warband Lodge
levels.description: A lodge for sworn warriors who winter together, feast together, and fight shoulder to shoulder come spring.

levels.name: Chosen Warriors' Hall
levels.description: The best of every clan train here under scarred champions. Their oaths bind them to the death of the last man.

levels.name: Field Clearings
levels.description: Stumps burned, stones piled into boundary walls, first furrows cut. The land begins to pay its keep.

levels.name: Village Granaries
levels.description: Raised granaries keep the harvest dry and the rats hungry. A village that stores grain survives a bad year.

levels.name: Ox-Plough Estates
levels.description: Heavy ploughs and ox teams break soil the old scratch-ploughs never touched. Yields climb, and so do rents.

levels.name: Canal-Fed Fields
levels.description: Ditches and sluices carry water to fields that once gambled on rain. Two crops a year where there was one.

levels.name: Great Estates
levels.description: Vast consolidated estates worked by gangs of laborers, feeding the city and enriching a very few. The countryside empties into the streets.

levels.name: Flood Basin Plots
levels.description: Low earthen banks trap the inundation in feeding basins. The river does the ploughman's hardest work for him.

levels.name: Shaduf Gardens
levels.description: Counterweighted sweeps lift river water to gardens above the flood line. Onions, flax, and fodder all year round.

levels.name: Nile Granaries
levels.description: Whitewashed granary courts tally the god-given surplus. Egypt's wealth is counted in baskets, not coins.

levels.name: Canal Network
levels.description: Dredged canals and regulated sluices push the black land outward year by year. Surveyors re-measure it all after every flood.

levels.name: Royal Granary Estates
levels.description: Crown estates run by ministries of grain, feeding cities and fleets from the richest farmland under the sun.

levels.name: Slash-and-Burn Plots
levels.description: Ash-fertilized clearings hacked from the forest edge, worked until the soil tires and the axes move on.

levels.name: Clan Fields
levels.description: Permanent strip fields divided among the clans, with barley for bread and beer in careful proportion.

levels.name: Cattle Runs
levels.description: Fenced pasture and droving paths for the herds that are a tribe's true treasury. Wealth here has legs.

levels.name: Remount Paddock
levels.description: Fenced pasture and a farrier's shed supplying horses to those citizens rich enough to ride to war.

levels.name: Equites' Stables
levels.description: Proper stables and a riding ring for the equestrian class. The horses are better bred than some of the riders.

levels.name: Cavalry School
levels.description: Riding masters, many of them hired Greeks and Gauls, drill squadrons in wheeling and pursuit. Rome buys the skills it lacks.

levels.name: Horse Corral
levels.description: Every family keeps horses; the corral just keeps them in one place. Children ride before they walk well.

levels.name: Breeder's Stables
levels.description: Bloodlines are tracked as carefully as genealogies. A good stallion is worth a village's yearly tribute.

levels.name: Nisean Stud Farm
levels.description: Tall Nisean horses, bred to carry an armored man all day, graze under armed guard. Kings send gifts to the stablemaster.

levels.name: Cataphract Stables
levels.description: Armories of scale barding beside the stalls, and a training ground where horse and rider learn to become one iron beast.

levels.name: Horse Paddock
levels.description: A modest paddock supplying mounts for scouts and dispatch riders. Cavalry is an expensive afterthought here.

levels.name: Citizen Cavalry Stables
levels.description: Stables maintained at public expense for the wealthy young men who form the city's mounted arm.

levels.name: Royal Stables
levels.description: Crown stables of imported bloodstock with grooms, veterinarians, and drillmasters to match. Squadrons here ride knee to knee.

levels.name: Horse Pens
levels.description: Hardy ponies penned by wattle fencing, sure-footed on hills that would lame a parade horse.

levels.name: Chieftain's Stables
levels.description: The chief's picked riders train and stable their mounts together, ready to strike wherever the war horn calls.

levels.name: Practice Butts
levels.description: Straw targets at ever-greater ranges. Here the bow is not a skill but an inheritance.

levels.name: Bowyer's Range
levels.description: Master bowyers season horn and sinew beside the range, matching each archer to a bow that fits like a glove.

levels.name: Master Bowmen's Field
levels.description: Champions shoot at gallop-speed marks for silver rings while boys watch and burn to match them.

levels.name: Skirmishers' Field
levels.description: Javelins and slings for the young and the poor, who learn to sting and scatter before the lines close.

levels.name: Archery Grounds
levels.description: A walled range with paid instructors, many of them Cretan. Massed volleys are drilled by trumpet call.

levels.name: Hunters' Range
levels.description: Marksmen who feed their families with bow and sling need little teaching to aim at men instead.

levels.name: War Hunters' Lodge
levels.description: The best hunters winter together, trading tricks of wind, range, and ambush that no drillmaster teaches.

levels.name: Engineers' Yard
levels.description: Sawpits, seasoned timber, and men who think in angles. Rams and mantlets take shape between contracts for bridges.

levels.name: Ballista Works
levels.description: Torsion springs of hair and sinew are wound and tested here. A well-tuned ballista threads a bolt through a window at two hundred paces.

levels.name: Great Engine Works
levels.description: Halls where master engineers build wall-breakers on geometric principle, and their smiths turn out finer edges for the army besides.

levels.name: Street Market
levels.description: Stalls, awnings, and shouted prices on fixed market days. Coin begins to displace barter.

levels.name: Trading House
levels.description: A roofed exchange where merchants store goods, settle debts, and hire caravans. Strangers' coin is weighed, not trusted.

levels.name: Merchants' Quarter
levels.description: Whole streets of warehouses, moneychangers, and foreign factors. Three languages are spoken before breakfast.

levels.name: Great Market Hall
levels.description: A colonnaded hall where bulk grain, metal, and cloth change hands by contract. The city's pulse is counted here in cartloads.

levels.name: Great Emporium
levels.description: An emporium famous across the sea, drawing goods from lands most citizens cannot name. Fortunes are made and lost by the tide table.

levels.name: Punic Bazaar
levels.description: Tin, dye, ivory, and salt fish under one clamorous roof. The Punic trader's scales are honest; his prices are not.

levels.name: Caravan Yard
levels.description: A walled yard where desert caravans meet the coastal trade, and goods from beyond the maps change hands at dawn.

levels.name: Merchant Princes' Hall
levels.description: The great families pool cargoes and split risks in marble offices. A sealed tablet here can move a fleet.

levels.name: House of Ledgers
levels.description: Rows of clerks track debts from Gades to Tyre. It is said no cargo sails the western sea unrecorded here.

levels.name: Emporium of the West
levels.description: The clearinghouse of half the world's silver, where every trade wind ends and every price begins.

levels.name: Barter Ground
levels.description: Hides for salt, iron for amber, on ground held sacred against feuds. Trade is truce made profitable.

levels.name: Trade Post
levels.description: A permanent post where southern merchants pay in wine and silver coin. The chief takes his tithe at the gate.

levels.name: Oppidum Market
levels.description: A true market town within the ramparts, striking its own coinage and drawing traders from a month's ride away.

levels.name: Graded Way
levels.description: Surveyed, ditched, and cambered so carts roll in any weather. The straight line is a Roman argument.

levels.name: Stone-Paved Way
levels.description: Fitted paving over deep foundations, with milestones counting the distance to the forum. Legions march twenty miles and complain about the food, not the road.

levels.name: Great Trunk Road
levels.description: A monumental highway with bridges, cuttings, and posting stations. Empires are held together by exactly this.

levels.name: Cart Tracks
levels.description: Worn ruts improved with gravel and fords marked with posts. Not glorious, but the mules approve.

levels.name: Stone Causeways
levels.description: Paved causeways over the wet ground and cut ramps through the passes, with waystations a day's travel apart.

levels.name: Ridgeway Trails
levels.description: High, dry paths along the ridgelines, cleared and marked by the tribes. Invaders prefer the valleys; that is the point.

levels.name: Fishing Wharf
levels.description: A timber jetty, drying racks, and the first customs officer, universally despised. Coastal traders begin to call.

levels.name: Stone Quays
levels.description: Stone moles shelter deep-hulled merchantmen, and cranes swing amphorae ashore by the hundred.

levels.name: Grand Harbor
levels.description: Breakwaters, a lighthouse, and berths for a hundred ships. Sailors say you can smell the money from the roadstead.

levels.name: Trading Wharf
levels.description: Punic shipmasters make port pay from the first plank. Even the fishing boats carry a little cargo on the side.

levels.name: Double Quays
levels.description: Paired quays work loading and unloading at once, turning ships around before rival ports have finished the paperwork.

levels.name: Circular Cothon
levels.description: An engineered ring-harbor in the famous Punic style, its sheltered basin ranked with berths. The city's true crown is made of water.

levels.name: Beach Landing
levels.description: Hulls drawn up on the shingle and a stone slip for heavy loads. Traders beach at dawn and are gone by dusk.

levels.name: Boat Sheds
levels.description: Sheds where hulls dry out of the sun and shipwrights lay keels for coastal galleys.

levels.name: Shipwright's Slipways
levels.description: Ramped slipways and seasoned timber stores turn out war galleys to a proven pattern. Crews drill on rowing frames ashore.

levels.name: Naval Arsenal
levels.description: A state arsenal of covered slips, rope walks, and bronze foundries that can lay down a squadron in a season.

levels.name: Ship Sheds
levels.description: Even a small Punic yard builds to templates refined over centuries. The sea is the one craft Carthage will not hire out.

levels.name: Fleet Slipways
levels.description: Numbered, prefabricated timbers let these slipways replace a lost hull faster than an enemy can celebrate sinking it.

levels.name: Grand Naval Arsenal
levels.description: The covered war-harbor's inner ring: admiral's island, drydocks, and shipwrights whose fathers' fathers did this work. Fleets are born here fully drilled.

levels.name: Cloaca Drains
levels.description: Stone-lined drains carry filth away beneath the streets. Unlovely, unseen, and worth more than a temple in a wet year.

levels.name: Bath House
levels.description: Hot rooms, cold plunges, and gossip for the price of a small coin. The city scrubs itself clean daily.

levels.name: City Aqueduct
levels.description: Arches stride across the valley bringing sweet water by the river-load. Fountains run in every quarter, and fevers grow rare.

levels.name: Public Fountains
levels.description: Clean water piped to fountain houses in each quarter, ending the long walk to the river and half the summer's fluxes.

levels.name: Bathing Courts
levels.description: Public washing courts and covered drains, kept by civic endowment. Physicians take students in the shade of the porticoes.

levels.name: City Cisterns
levels.description: Vast covered cisterns and settling tanks secure the water supply against drought, siege, and the diseases of crowds.

levels.name: Spring Well
levels.description: A stone-lined well over a guarded spring, ringed with offerings. Clean water is holy, and holiness keeps it clean.

levels.name: Fighting Pit
levels.description: A timber-fenced pit where paired fighters settle wagers in blood. The crowd forgets the grain price for an afternoon.

levels.name: Sand Arena
levels.description: Banked wooden seating around a proper sand floor, with beast hunts on festival days. Magistrates buy popularity by the bout.

levels.name: Grand Circus
levels.description: A monumental racing circuit seating tens of thousands. Chariot factions command loyalties that generals envy.

levels.name: Odeon
levels.description: A small roofed hall for music, recitation, and civic prize-givings. The town discovers it has opinions about poets.

levels.name: Open-Air Theatre
levels.description: Stone tiers set into the hillside, where the whole city weeps at tragedies and howls at comedies about its own councilmen.

levels.name: Festival Precinct
levels.description: Theatre, processional way, and games-ground in one precinct, filling the calendar with festivals the poor attend free.

levels.name: Feasting Hall
levels.description: Roast meat, strong beer, and boasting contests under one smoky roof. Grudges are settled or at least postponed.

levels.name: Festival Grounds
levels.description: A great ground for horse races, wrestling, and the seasonal gatherings where the whole people remembers it is one people.

levels.name: Scribal School
levels.description: Boys copy contracts and maxims until their letters are fit for court. A literate city argues on paper instead of in the street.

levels.name: Hall of Philosophers
levels.description: Hired lecturers teach rhetoric, geometry, and the art of governing men. Future magistrates make useful friends here.

levels.name: Great Library
levels.description: Tens of thousands of scrolls, resident scholars, and copyists working by lamplight. Kings compete to be its patron.

levels.name: Execution Grounds
levels.description: A stark public ground where sentences are carried out before witnesses. The lesson is brutal, and it is learned.

levels.name: Silver Diggings
levels.description: Open trenches follow the bright veins into the hillside, and the assayer's furnace never cools.

levels.name: Deep Silver Galleries
levels.description: Timbered shafts, drainage wheels, and gangs working by lamplight far underground. The mint upstairs sets the pace.

levels.name: Iron Pits
levels.description: Ore pits and charcoal-hungry bloomeries smoking on the hillside. Every smith in the region buys from these fires.

levels.name: Iron Galleries
levels.description: Driven galleries and ranks of furnaces feed a trade in blooms and billets that armies quietly depend upon.

levels.name: Gold Diggings
levels.description: Panners and pit gangs chase the bright seams; what they raise goes straight to the treasury.

levels.name: Deep Gold Mine
levels.description: Timbered shafts follow the vein into the hill. Torches gutter, ore baskets rise, and the mint never sleeps.
